first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent me this and I expected pretty beach photos and nothing else. Instead the first thing it tells me is whether the marriage is legal and that hurricane season should decide the date. That is the sensible order. I kept going, top to bottom, the way I always do.

journey.quote: Either way, the hurricane season, the drier months and your guests' long journey from Australia should shape the date before anything else does.
journey.reaction: Good. Someone is thinking about the guests and the weather before the flowers. That is what I'd be asking about.

journey.section: Who Punta Cana suits, and who it does not
journey.quote: It asks more of couples with older relatives or young families travelling from Australia, because the journey is long and the heat is real.
journey.reaction: Thank you for saying it plainly. My mother is 86. I appreciate not being sold a fantasy.

journey.section: Documents the civil registry asks foreigners for
journey.quote: Without one, the marriage is recorded under community of property.
journey.reaction: Now that is something my husband will want to read. I'd never have known to ask. It's a little alarming, but I'd rather know.

journey.quote: Any document not in Spanish must be translated by a judicial interpreter and legalised by the Dominican Attorney General's Office; in some cases the translation can be done at a Dominican consulate and legalised at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
journey.reaction: This is exactly my worry about paperwork in another language. It's clear enough, but it makes the symbolic ceremony at home sound far less trouble. I'd be nudging my daughter that way.

journey.quote: The registry booking, documents and timing remain your responsibility, so build them into your plan from the start.
journey.reaction: Honest, and I respect that. But it does make me ask what, exactly, the Advisor is responsible for. The page tells me what isn't theirs more clearly than what is.

journey.section: Entry, tourist card and travel advice
journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller's advice for the Dominican Republic is to exercise a high degree of caution, due to the threat of violent crime.
journey.reaction: That stopped me. I'm glad it's here rather than hidden, but my husband will read this line first and say no. I'd want to hear how people manage this in practice.

journey.section: Entry, tourist card and travel advice
journey.quote: Australia has no embassy in the Dominican Republic.
journey.reaction: Who do I ring at 2am if Mum has a fall? This answers part of it, through Canada, but it doesn't make me feel better.

journey.quote: Choose comprehensive cover that includes medical evacuation, because the Australian Government won't pay those costs.
journey.reaction: Practical and plain. This is the sort of detail that tells me the writer has thought about real families.

journey.quote: Ask how older guests reach the ceremony on sand, how far it is from their rooms and where they can sit out of the heat between events.
journey.reaction: Yes. This is my mother. I'd only add walking frames and wheelchairs by name, because sand and a walking frame don't mix.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, and works in your time zone with quotes in AUD.
journey.reaction: This is the line I was looking for. In writing, in Australian dollars, in our time zone. I'd underline it for my husband.

journey.quote: These are the questions to put to any venue, in writing.
journey.reaction: A good list, but nothing on contracts or deposits. Is the deposit protected? What currency is the contract in? Those are my first two questions and they aren't on it.

journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor works with you from start to finish, as your single point of contact.
journey.reaction: One person accountable is what I want. I'd still want a name and a phone call before anything is paid.

unanswered_questions: Is the deposit protected, and what happens to it if the venue cancels or a hurricane closes the resort?
What language and currency are the venue contracts written in, and who reads them on our behalf?
Who do we ring if something goes wrong during the trip, out of hours?
Can a guest with a walking frame or wheelchair get to a beach ceremony at all?
Can I, as the parent who is paying, be on the first call with my daughter?
What exactly does the Wedded Advisor take responsibility for, as opposed to the couple?
How long would the legal paperwork take from start to finish, roughly, so we know when to begin?

turn_offs_found.quote: These are the questions to put to any venue, in writing.
turn_offs_found.why: The list that follows never mentions contracts, deposits, refunds or who is responsible. That is one of the things that makes me close a page.

would_share_with: My husband, with the Smartraveller paragraph and the separation of property line highlighted
My daughter, to say the symbolic ceremony at home looks simpler

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, and works in your time zone with quotes in AUD.
cta_reaction.why: The written inclusions and AUD quotes are reassuring, and I'd be happy to have a conversation. But I'd want to know it starts with a phone call and that someone will talk me through deposits before I hand over our details. The page doesn't say how the first contact works.

Suggested edit: old "The registry booking, documents and timing remain your responsibility, so build them into your plan from the start." new "The registry booking, documents and timing remain your responsibility, so build them into your plan from the start.

### Contracts, deposits and who to call

Ask what language and currency the venue contract is written in, how deposits are paid and what is refunded if plans change. Ask who your contact is on the day, and how to reach them out of hours."

Name mobility aids in the older guests questions. Suggested edit: old "Ask how older guests reach the ceremony on sand, how far it is from their rooms and where they can sit out of the heat between events." new "Ask how older guests reach the ceremony on sand, how far it is from their rooms and where they can sit out of the heat between events. Ask whether paths, ramps and seating suit a guest using a walking frame or wheelchair."

Make it clear the Advisor is the person to talk this through with, including families helping to pay, without promising anything new. Can the closing section say how first contact works (for example a phone call) if the brand confirms it? Not added here because it is not stated in the draft.
